title: FastTurn: micro-session templates — sketch journal
body:
Quick context (brain-dump):

Goal: prototype a small product surface that lets product teams assemble and ship ultra-short conversational flows (2–6 turns) as composable 'micro-templates' that optimize for latency, token cost, and predictable quality. Target use-cases: onboarding tips, inline help, confirmation dialogs, guided data collection, short transactional assistants.

Why this now:
- Customers keep asking for cheaper, faster ways to embed assistant-like flows into UI chrome (not full chat).
- We have runtime gains (KV caching + smaller generation models) that make tiny flows cheap — but no first-class UX or API for composing them.
- Opportunity: create an opinionated template layer that maps cleanly to our billing/SLAs and routing (hosted/dedicated).

Key ideas / feature atoms:
1) Template manifest: name, intent, max-turns (default 4), cost-tier suggestion (fast/cheap / balanced / high-fidelity), model hints.
2) Compact invocation API: POST /templates/execute {template_id, user_inputs, session_id (optional), quality_hint}. Response streams minimal payload: decisions, final_text, tokens_used.
3) Localizable content blocks: static text + small variable placeholders + optional canonical examples (for evals).
4) Fallback policies: if primary model unavailable, fall back to simpler template + canned response; explicit fallback chain attached to template.
5) Billing leash: per-template token budgets and enforced max latency (e.g., 200–500ms p90) — auto-route to cheaper model if over budget.
6) Developer DX: web-based template editor (WYSIWYG) -> exports JSON manifest + test harness -> quick install snippet.

User stories (short):
- As a product PM, I want a template for 'collect-email-and-consent' so I can insert it into sign-up flow and guarantee low latency and predictable cost.
- As an SRE, I want templates to declare preferred model families so I can route low-tier templates to quantized models and keep p99 latency within SLA.
- As an engineer, I want an SDK helper that rehydrates template placeholders and handles retry/fallback transparently.

Acceptance signals (MVP):
- Can create and deploy a template via console in < 10 minutes.
- Average cost per completed template <= target cost bucket (e.g., 3–5x cheaper than full-chat baseline).
- p95 latency under configured threshold for 'fast' templates in hosted regions.
- Integration tests + 3 customer beta use cases (onboarding, in-app help, simple checkout).

Architecture sketch (notes):
- Template manifest stored in control plane (small JSON blobs) + immutable versions.
- Execution path: controller validates manifest -> picks model variant by routing policy -> runtime uses prefix caching (shared prompt skeleton) -> continuous batching window tuned to tiny sessions.
- Telemetry hooks: token breakdown per-template, per-turn latency, fallback occurrence, quality regressions tied to example set.

Operational knobs to expose:
- Max-tokens-per-invocation (hard cap).
- Quality_hint: low/medium/high (influences model family selection).
- Fallback chain (ordered list of compatible model variants).
- Circuit-breaker threshold (fail fast to canned response if queue depth or latency degraded).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Pricing model: per-template monthly retainer vs strictly per-token. Customers using many micro-templates may prefer simpler pricing; need estimate of how many micro-templates typical app would create.
- UX vs API: do we require template creation via Console (good for safety) or allow programmatic manifests (developer freedom)? Hybrid?
- Quality monitoring: how to attach small, meaningful eval sets to tiny templates? Could be a lightweight A/B harness with few golden prompts.
- Internationalization: templates will need pluralization/locale variables — manifest complexity increases.

Prototype plan (2 sprints):
Sprint 1 (explore + smoke):
- Minimal manifest spec (fields above)
- CLI/REST minimal execute endpoint (no editor) + runtime routing to two model tiers (fast/standard)
- Basic telemetry (tokens, latency), simple fallback to canned response
- Internal dogfood: integrate 2 Redwood internal flows (docs assistant snippet + quick onboarding)

Sprint 2 (polish + console):
- Simple template editor in Console (create, test, publish)
- SDK helper + example snippets (React + mobile)
- Beta onboarding with 3 customer teams, collect cost + quality signals

Metrics to watch:
- Templates created per tenant
- Average tokens consumed per template run
- Fallback rate (%)
- Time-to-serve (p50/p90/p99)
- Customer engagement: percent of templates reused across pages

Next steps (me):
- Wireframe quick editor (paper mocks by EOW)
- Talk to two AE/customer champions to validate pricing sensitivity (this week)
- Spike JIRA-branch for manifest storage and lightweight execute path

Random nit-notes / UX thoughts:
- Templates should support 'handoff points' — ability to escalate to full chat session and import prior micro-turns into full context.
- Editor should surface estimated cost per run as you edit (rough token estimate + model selection).
- Consider a 'composable step' library (form-fill, confirm, multi-choice) so non-devs can assemble templates.

Rough risks:
- Too many tiny templates could increase control-plane metadata volume; need GC/versioning strategy.
- Customers may misuse templates for complex flows leading to poor quality expectations.
- Unexpected cross-tenant caching semantics when templates share prompt skeletons (privacy checks).

---
Raw sketch ends. This is deliberately rough — notes to self. Will refine into a light PRD once initial customer reactions and a small runtime spike are done.
